title: Slices from the inside: capacity, growth and `make()`

videos.script: Lesson 11 showed that a slice is a view over an array, with a length and a capacity. This lesson is about the second number. {{lencap}} First, what each one allows. You can index up to the length, and you can stretch a slice up to its capacity. Go past either one and the program stops. {{grow}} Then append. When the array is full, append makes a bigger one and copies everything across. You will watch the capacities a real run printed, and read the rule in the runtime's own source. {{make}} Next, make. Telling Go the size up front saves every one of those copies. And an empty slice is not always a nil one, which JSON makes plain. {{alias}} Last, the bug this lesson exists for. Two slices share an array, one of them appends, and the other one changes under your feet. By the end you can say when append copies, and when it writes into somebody else's elements.
